epic.title: Time allocation tracker: question round first
epic.description:
Rob Dyrdek's time allocation system built into Mycelium: calendar time colour-coded into categories (work, family, health, personal) against weekly targets, with a quarterly review. The question round comes first and settles the categories, the targets and where the hours come from. Owner-only, in Phil's personal space.

## Order
tracker.01 (the question round, one sitting), then tracker.02 (the build, which also waits for the Google reconnect MYC-181), then tracker.03 every quarter.

## Done means
The tracker shows a real week against targets and the first quarterly review is done.

## Flags
- [claude] flagged once: section 11b dropped "what next" as a 2027 priority and named "I kept building it instead of using it" as the risk; this is a new build. Not reopened.

## Dossier
The dossier is attached in Docs: (link filled by the integrator).

tickets.title: Question round: which categories, what weekly targets, where the hours come from (calendar, Four-Day Week tracker, PC worker)
tickets.description:
## What
One 15-minute sitting answering the questions below on this ticket, before anything is built. (1) Categories: work, family, health, personal as the brief says, or others; is sleep a category (Rob Dyrdek's published split counts it: roughly 30% sleep, 30% family, 30% work, 10% health in one telling, though public figures vary)? (2) A weekly target per category, in hours. (3) Where each category's hours come from: Google Calendar events (by calendar, by colour, or by a keyword in the title), the Four-Day Week tracker's logged hours for work (no start times, so totals only), the PC worker's active time, or the Apple Watch for sleep. One source per category, so nothing counts twice. (4) Colours per category. (5) Whether a daily one-to-ten score (Dyrdek scores life, work and health daily) is wanted or not. (6) Owner-only and off the wall, unless Phil says otherwise.

## Why
H5: build the time allocation tracker in Mycelium "with a question round first (which categories, what targets, where the hours come from)".

## Done looks like
Every question answered on this ticket in a line each.

## Unlocks
tracker.02 (the build reads these answers).

## Depends on
Nothing.

## Flag
[claude] flagged once: section 11b dropped "what next" as a 2027 priority and named "I kept building it instead of using it" as the risk; this is a new build. Not reopened.

tickets.title: Build: calendar time colour-coded into categories against weekly targets
tickets.description:
## What
Build the tracker from tracker.01's answers: a page (under Organisation, next to Hours) showing this week's hours per category against its weekly target, colour-coded as chosen, with last week alongside and a simple quarter view for the review. Hours come from the sources tracker.01 picks: Google Calendar events mapped to categories (read on page load and in the daily job, as Vercel Hobby allows daily crons only), the Four-Day Week tracker's `hours_entries` totals for work if chosen, and any other source he picked. Every figure is derived, never stored (the pattern `lib/hours` uses). Personal space, owner-only, never shared by a team grant, off the wall unless tracker.01 says otherwise.

## Why
H5: "calendar time colour-coded into categories (work, family, health, personal) against weekly targets".

## Done looks like
The page shows the current week with each category's hours and target from real calendar data; a category with no source shows as "no source" rather than zero; tests for the week boundary and the category mapping pass; `next build` green.

## Unlocks
tracker.03 (the quarterly review reads the quarter view).

## Depends on
tracker.01 (the answers); MYC-181 (Google reconnect: the calendar sync has been unproven since the token expired on 2026-06-24).

## Red team
- Finding 41: The build starts after the capture habit has held for 30 days (brain.26).

tickets.title: Quarterly review
tickets.description:
## What
Every quarter, one 15-minute sitting on the tracker's quarter view: which categories met their weekly target most weeks, which did not, whether the targets still fit, and one change for the next quarter (a target, a category, or none). Also one question about use: was the tracker opened most weeks? If not, the review says so plainly and the next step is to use it, not to build more.

## Why
H5: "with a quarterly review"; and Phil's own named risk, "I kept building it instead of using it".

## Done looks like
Each quarter: the review's fields filled on the guide and any target change saved in the tracker's settings.

## Unlocks
Nothing.

## Depends on
tracker.02 (the build and its quarter view).
